title: Citizen helpline speech-to-text across India's languages
business_question: A state or national citizen helpline takes calls in many Indian languages: which speech-to-text works in all of them, and how bad is its weakest language?

dataset.name: FLEURS (google/fleurs) test split
dataset.how_made: First 25 distinct sentences of at most 30 s (in archive order) of each Indic FLEURS test set, real volunteers reading Wikipedia sentences; reference = FLEURS raw_transcription.

metrics.name: WER in the system's WORST language
WER in the WORST language, excluding languages output in another script
Clips with no transcript at all (blocked/empty after retries)

findings: In the 13 languages where its output script matches FLEURS, saaras:v3 has the lowest WER in 12 (all except Urdu; Nepali 0.271 vs 0.272 and Telugu 0.170 vs 0.173 are ties; on CER Gemini wins Telugu, Marathi and Urdu): macro WER 0.17 / CER 0.052 vs gemini-3.8-flash 0.21 / 0.090, gpt-4o-transcribe 0.27 / 0.090, whisper-1 (hosted) 0.79 / 0.54 and whisper-large-v3-turbo (local) 0.75 / 0.45. Biggest saaras leads: Assamese 0.16 vs 0.31, Malayalam 0.17 vs 0.27, Punjabi 0.15 vs 0.23 (Gemini figures include its blocked clips).

Worst language: saaras Nepali 0.27 [0.22-0.33], Gemini Assamese 0.31 [0.21-0.42], Whisper Malayalam 1.00. Gemini's worst-language CI overlaps saaras's, so on read speech the two are close on the weakest language; Whisper is not.

gpt-4o-transcribe is the most robust OpenAI option and the only system besides Gemini that writes every language, including Sindhi, in the reference script: WER worst language Nepali 0.42 [0.32-0.53], best CER of all systems on Tamil (0.091), zero blocked clips, p50 1.4 s (RTF 0.12). Its WER trails saaras in 12 of 13 comparable languages (it wins only Urdu, and on CER also Tamil); the gap is mostly word boundaries and spelling choices — its macro CER (0.090) equals Gemini's.

Sindhi: saaras:v3 (language_code sd-IN) writes Sindhi in Devanagari, FLEURS uses Perso-Arabic script, so it scores WER 0.996 here. The Devanagari text reads as a faithful transcript (e.g. 'होस्टाइल माहौल वारे कोर्स…' for 'هوسٽائل ماحول واري ڪورس…'), so this is a script choice, not deafness — but a helpline that needs Arabic-script Sindhi cannot get it from saaras. Gemini handles Sindhi in Arabic script at WER 0.21.

Gemini returned no transcript at all for 20 of 350 clips on the first try (prompt blocked, block_reason OTHER) and for 11 (3.1%) even after three attempts, spread over 7 languages (Assamese 3, Punjabi 2, Malayalam 2, Bengali, Tamil, Kannada, Odia 1 each). On the clips it did transcribe, its macro WER is 0.185. A helpline using Gemini needs a fallback for blocked audio.

Hosted whisper-1 rejects language codes bn, te, gu, pa ('Language 'bn' is not supported.', HTTP 400) and has no Odia, so those ran on auto-detect; it then wrote Bengali, Gujarati, Malayalam, Odia, Punjabi and Sindhi mostly in the wrong script, and Assamese/Telugu at CER >= 0.5. Only Hindi (0.30) and Urdu (0.24) are usable — no better than the local model.

Whisper-large-v3-turbo cannot serve five of the fourteen languages: with the language forced it still wrote Punjabi in Devanagari (23/25), Assamese in Devanagari (18/25), Malayalam in Devanagari or Kannada script (23/25), and Sindhi mostly in Devanagari; it has no Odia at all and auto-detect wrote Odia audio in Gujarati script (20/25). Only Urdu (0.21) and Hindi (0.28) are usable.

Speed per clip (5-30 s of audio): saaras p50 0.87 s / p95 2.3 s (RTF 0.09); gpt-4o-transcribe 1.4 / 2.2 s (RTF 0.12); whisper-1 3.0 / 6.6 s (RTF 0.28); Gemini 3.9 / 7.0 s (RTF 0.36); local Whisper p50 8.6 s (RTF 0.84) on a GPU shared with a 30B llama.cpp server.

saaras:v3 REST rejects clips over 30 s ('use the batch API'), so long callers must be chunked or sent through the job API. 74 calls first ended as HTTP 400 'Failed to read the file'; these followed 429 rate-limit retries in common/bench.py, which re-sends an already-read file handle (an empty upload), and all succeeded when the file was re-opened per attempt.

Cost: 350 clips (72.6 min) cost Rs 36.3 on saaras at the Rs 30/hour list price; Gemini used 116k input / 16k output tokens, gpt-4o-transcribe 47k input / 20k output tokens, whisper-1 72.6 billed minutes for the same audio.
caveats: FLEURS is read Wikipedia sentences recorded by volunteers on decent microphones: easier than real helpline calls (spontaneous speech, code-mixing, 8 kHz phone lines, background noise). Expect higher error rates in production, and see uc01 for phone-line and code-mixed results.

25 clips per language (first 25 distinct sentences <= 30 s in archive order); per-language CIs are wide (often +/-0.05 to +/-0.10 WER). Rankings between saaras and Gemini inside one language are often not significant; the macro averages and Whisper's failures are.
Urdu is FLEURS ur_pk (Pakistani speakers) and Nepali is ne_np; Indian Urdu/Nepali speakers may differ.
WER on Indic text is harsh: agglutinative words, optional nukta/halant spellings and number formatting all count as errors. CER is the fairer cross-language number; both are reported.

Sindhi is scored against Perso-Arabic references only; nothing is transliterated, so saaras's Devanagari Sindhi is counted as wrong. The 'excluding other-script languages' worst-language metric shows the result without it.
Gemini's blocked clips count as WER 1.0. FLEURS sentences come from Wikipedia, so the block may be a recitation/content filter that real calls would trigger less often — unverified.
Whisper latency was measured on a shared Mac whose GPU was also serving other benchmark jobs.
verdict: For a multi-language citizen helpline, saaras:v3 is the strongest default: lowest WER in 12 of the 13 comparable languages (several near-ties), macro CER about half of Gemini's and gpt-4o-transcribe's, every clip transcribed, and answers in under a second. Plan for its two gaps: it writes Sindhi only in Devanagari, and it accepts at most 30 s per REST call. Gemini-3.8-flash (worst language Assamese 0.31) and gpt-4o-transcribe (worst Nepali 0.42, never blocks, 1.4 s) are the credible alternatives and both handle Arabic-script Sindhi; Gemini silently returned nothing for about 3% of clips. Whisper — hosted whisper-1 or local large-v3-turbo — is not fit for an Indian helpline: it rejects or mis-scripts six of the fourteen languages.
